The note carried on for a long time before Bailey finally ended the song she was singing and immediately started to beam at the sea of praise faceless people gave her. Like they were supposed to because she was that good—if the thousands of fans worldwide were anything to go off of. It was the bare minimum, to sing her praise and worship her music after all the hard work she put into it, but that was beside the point.

She panted out heavily as wild, dark eyes ran through the crowd of fans—*her* fans—before landing on the bar just behind them. There sat only a few people who either just showed up to the pub, or grew tired of the show and needed to rest. Perfect time to get herself something as well since she had worked herself up all night. So as the crowd began to chant for an encore to the last performance, Bailey jumped down from the stage—ignoring the muttered comment Gunnar made under his breath about her drinking again—before slamming her hand down on the counter and barking her order at the bartender for an “Old Fashioned.”

Taking a seat down at one of the stools, Bailey fixed the older man with a sharp, bored glare as she drummed her fingers on the table surface, keeping an eye on what he was doing just so she could call him out on the mistake when it happened. That was one of her favorite things about this pub, she could be a dick to the workers and they still always allowed her back in.

Why? Simple answer. Her band, Strip Teaser, was the sole reason this place didn’t go to shit, so banning her would be setting the place up to fail. Oh, and Milo was fucking loaded. One call to his dad and this place and the surrounding area would be turned into a shopping mall where preteens went to get their first piercing at Claire’s and parents tried not to have a heart attack about their kids being converted into unholy Goths that sin against the lord or whatever.

Finally, the drink was placed in front of her with a loud grunt from the bartender before she moved away from Bailey with a shake of his head, as if disappointed that he had to deal with her for more than a second. She sipped her drink slowly as she looked around the pub with a disinterested expression before turning to look at her bandmates just as Blake slipped away from where Gunnar and Milo were arguing over something she could only imagine was pointless.

Just then, someone took a seat right next to her and Bailey stared at them from the corner of her eye. There was plenty of room at the bar to sit down anywhere else, but they just *had* to sit next to her. It was pathetic how desperate they were for her, someone they would probably never actually get.

But still, she set her alcoholic beverage down and turned to face them head-on with a low growl of frustration and annoyance. “What? Has your mother never taught you staring is *rude*, or do you just like having your eyes ripped out from the sockets?” She hissed out as a grin slowly grew on her face at the thought of their screams and cries. “You know, if you want to be taught that lesson, I am more than happy to teach it to you. We could go to the bathroom in the back. Super quiet so no one would bother us.”
